Live on candidate 5df5f64 the operator reports a complete one-shot pairing transaction and then a single no-finger IDENTIFY whose epoch audit shows preflight_complete=1 with 7 read-only commands, tls=1, secure_e4_contract=MATCH, secure_failure=0, coordinator_source=2, zero_seed=1, fdt_samples=3, first_image=0, persistent=0, pairing_writes=0, pairing_prepared=0, pairing_e0_reserved=0, pairing_tls=1, pairing_active=0, pairing_active_reused=1, real_submit=91, outstanding=0, drained=1, context_closed=1. Canonical P6 item 7, the ordinary ACTIVE reopen with zero E0, is therefore PROVEN on the target: the reader was reused through the state-v2 ACTIVE record with no durable sensor or host write and a clean drain/close. Item 6, the zero-seed FDT no-finger bootstrap, is not yet proven: three IRQ 0x0100 samples were accepted, which confirms on the target that the corrected first-sample boundary accepts a nonzero touch mask, but that audit could not distinguish a completed learning from a rejected third delta gate, because fdt_learned reports the terminal readiness flag that cancellation clears. The three requested clarifications are answered from code. (1) fdt_learned maps to post_tls.learned_fdt_ready, set only at the third sample and reset by lifecycle_fail, which goodix_post_tls_lifecycle_cancel calls; the monotonic fresh_fdt_count and the delta counters are not reset, so the final 0 was a post-cancel audit artifact and the audit now exposes fdt_learned_once, fdt_delta_within, fdt_delta_outside, fdt36_submits and the baseline image counters. (2) coordinator_decision=1 was stale telemetry: the epoch acquires the legacy owner first without live evidence, which sets READY_LEGACY, then the preflight finds the live validator mismatched, releases the legacy material and transfers ownership to the state-v2 pairing activation, which updated source and writer_enabled but not decision; the takeover is now recorded as STATE_V2_PAIRING_ACTIVATION, appended to the enum so previously recorded numeric values keep their meaning, and the new pairing_disposition token reports the real selector. The stale value was conservative in the only predicates that consult it. (3) pairing_writer maps to writer_enabled, set when a pairing activation instance is constructed and again at ready-TLS: it means the state-v2 writer path was armed and available, not that the writer was entered; entry is measured by pairing_prepared, pairing_e0_reserved, pairing_writes and the persistent sum, all zero here, with pairing_active_reused=1 and pairing_active=0 because REUSE_ACTIVE_TLS marks the TLS proof and skips promotion by design. Note that the host reopen entered through the pairing-activation reuse path because the legacy five-file material is still installed, while the offline integration fixture has no legacy material and reopens through the coordinator READY_ACTIVE path; both are zero-E0 and both are now separately identifiable in the audit. The FIRST_SAMPLE formulation is corrected everywhere: with a zero or stale reference the first manual sample may legitimately carry nonzero touch bits including all six, and those bits alone neither prove nor exclude a finger; no deterministic 0x003f claim remains.
